Alex 

Thanks for the diagram; added a few notes inline. High-level technical answers based on your questions:

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering
- We support both. PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoints) is our recommended approach for control-plane communications (management, metrics, auth) because it avoids exposing endpoints outside your VPC and simplifies security reviews.
- VPC peering is fine for high-throughput inference data paths; it can reduce latency but requires additional route entries. Either approach can be used concurrently (PrivateLink for control plane, peering for data plane).

2) Ports / protocols
- API/control traffic: HTTPS (443) only.
- Optional gRPC: 443 (TLS) if you choose gRPC; we do not require open non-TLS ports.
- No special ephemeral port ranges required for the basic setup; peering uses your existing VPC routing.

3) IP allowlist and static egress
- We can provide a small set of static outbound IPs (NAT) for callbacks and webhook-style integrations. If you need single /28 ranges, tell us which region and we'll propose a set.
- For inbound control plane access (PrivateLink), you'll create interface endpoints in your account and can restrict security groups to the interface endpoint(s) and any CIDRs you choose.

4) Route tables / TGW
- If you use a Transit Gateway (TGW), you will need to ensure the TGW routes the interface endpoint or peered VPC CIDRs to the appropriate VPC. Well include a short TGW checklist in the runbook.

Next steps (from engineering):
- I attached a short runbook excerpt and the standard port/CIDR recommendations.
- If you confirm PrivateLink + our static egress IP request, we can kick off an onboarding ticket and target a 3-week timeline from kickoff (includes security review and staging cutover).

Proposed owners: Marissa (Redwood SE) for technical onboarding, Sean for commercial.

-Marissa
